title: Reformat Date
statement:
The string `date` names a calendar day with three parts separated by single spaces: the day of the month as an English ordinal (`1st`, `2nd`, `3rd`, `4th`, ..., `30th`, `31st`), the month as a three-letter abbreviation (`Jan`, `Feb`, `Mar`, `Apr`, `May`, `Jun`, `Jul`, `Aug`, `Sep`, `Oct`, `Nov`, `Dec`), and a year between 1900 and 2100.

Return the same day written as `YYYY-MM-DD`: the four-digit year, the month number and the day number, with the month and the day each padded to two digits by a leading zero, joined by hyphens. The input is always a real date in this form, so no error handling is needed.
constraints: date has the form "Day Month Year" with single spaces
Month is one of Jan, Feb, Mar, Apr, May, Jun, Jul, Aug, Sep, Oct, Nov, Dec
date is a valid calendar date
notes:
## Intuition

The three pieces of the date can be converted on their own and glued back together in a new order. The year is already four digits. The month needs a lookup from its abbreviation to its position in the year. The day is a number followed by a two-letter ordinal ending (`st`, `nd`, `rd`, `th`), so dropping the last two characters leaves just the digits.

## Approach

1. Keep the twelve abbreviations in calendar order in `months`.
2. Split `date` on spaces into `dayText`, `monthText` and `year`.
3. Cut the two-letter ending off `dayText` to get `day`.
4. Find `monthText` in `months`; its index plus one is `month`.
5. Pad `day` and `month` to two characters with a leading `"0"`, then join year, month and day with hyphens.

## Example 1, step by step

`date = "20th Oct 2052"` splits into `"20th"`, `"Oct"` and `"2052"`. Removing `"th"` gives `day = "20"`. `"Oct"` sits at index 9, so `month = "10"`. Both already have two digits, so the result is `"2052-10-20"`. For Example 2, `"6th"` becomes `"6"`, padded to `"06"`, and `"Jun"` (index 5) becomes `"06"`, giving `"1933-06-06"`.

## Complexity

- Time: O(1): the input has at most 13 characters and the month table has 12 entries.
- Space: O(1): only a few short strings are built.

## Pitfalls

- Single-digit days and months need a leading zero: `"6"` must become `"06"`.
- Do not remove only one character from the day: every ending (`st`, `nd`, `rd`, `th`) is two letters long.
- `indexOf` is zero-based, so add one to get the month number.

## Variables

| Name | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `months` | the month abbreviations in calendar order |
| `dayText`, `monthText`, `year` | the three space-separated parts of `date` |
| `day` | the day digits with the ordinal ending removed |
| `month` | the month number as a string |
| `paddedDay`, `paddedMonth` | the day and month padded to two digits |

narration.2: List the month abbreviations in calendar order so a month's index tells its number.
narration.3: Split the date on spaces into its day, month and year parts.
narration.6: The year is already four digits, so it is used as it is.
narration.8: Every ordinal ending is two letters long, so dropping the last two characters leaves the day digits.
narration.9: The month's position in the list plus one is its number.
narration.11: Pad the day to two digits, so 6 becomes 06.
narration.12: Pad the month the same way.
narration.13: Join year, month and day with hyphens in YYYY-MM-DD order.
